_about: Colours for every solid of the RCC's meshes that take their colours from an atlas, keyed by the mesh names of our CAD export (rcc.glb), in each mesh's OWN coordinates in mm (rcc.glb mesh coordinates x 1000), in the form tools/build_model.py colour_from_atlas reads (bbox_min / bbox_max, solids {name, min, max, colour}). Two sources. (1) The meshes the RCC shares with the MRA (the joysticks, the Nano I/O module, the controller's Nano, and the car Nano's regulator, LEDs, capacitors, resistors and reset button, which have the same mesh names and geometry) are copied unchanged from colour-atlas-mra.json, TechBox's own Cadasio project for the MRA as Lee approved it: same CAD bodies in the same own frames, and every entry matches rcc.glb's solids at 100 % (checked 15 Oct 2026). The RCC Cadasio colours these parts differently (royal-blue shield, teal Nanos, pure black joystick board): see _skipped. (2) Meshes the MRA lacks, where TechBox's published RCC project (instructions.online 19075, read with tools/cadasio/atlas.py) has one solid per solid of ours and colours worth keeping: the FS90R wheel motor and the barrel plug's two lead stubs. Everything else on the RCC is coloured by rules in materials.json; the published colours not used, and why, are under _skipped.
_how_to_read: solids[*].min/max: for a solid that exists in our mesh ('solid' is its index as tools/build_model.py numbers connected components) these are OUR solid's box, and box_error_mm says how far Cadasio's box for the same body is from it (sum of the six face offsets).

solids[*].solid = null: a Cadasio body with no solid of its own in our mesh; min/max are then Cadasio's box moved into our mesh coordinates. 'inside_solid' names our solid whose box contains it (it was welded into that solid, or is a face copy lying on it).

skin = true: in our mesh this solid is an open shell lying within 0.05 mm of another solid (Cadasio name contains 'Surface-Offset'): a coloured face copy. The solid underneath must take the same colour or it shows through.
set_in_step = true: the colour was set in Cadasio (colour_main on the solid or an ancestor). false: Cadasio shows the SolidWorks colour (cad_colour) unchanged.

also_covers: Cadasio bodies of another colour that are part of this one solid in our mesh (they touch, so our split into connected solids cannot separate them). The colour given is that of the body whose box is nearest to the solid's.
shown = false: the author pushed this body under another surface, so it is not seen (servo label only).

Entries copied from the MRA keep the MRA's fields: 'solid' indices are the MRA mesh's numbering (rcc.glb is tessellated more coarsely and numbers some meshes' solids differently; the match is by boxes, so this does not matter), and 'instances' here lists the RCC instances that carry the mesh, with the MRA's in 'mra_instances'.

Entries from the RCC Cadasio ('source': 'rcc_cadasio') are tools/cadasio/atlas.py's output for that component: each solid's Cadasio box (identical to ours in the mesh's own frame, to 0.005 mm) and the colour it shows most often while visible; 'shown' is the number of visible steps.

materials.json may swap an atlas colour for a palette entry (a rule's atlas_colours): the FS90R's colours go through palette names so that one ruling from Lee changes them everywhere, and the lead stubs take the colours of the leads the player draws.

_conductors.note: Lead colours traced through rcc.glb by shared end points (15 Oct 2026), for the player's wires and the stubs on the parts.
_conductors.battery_lead: The CAD's battery lead (NAUO41 plugged, NAUO42 unplugged) has two conductors. The one leaving the battery clip (NAUO15 DC_Adaptor) from its stub at own z -1.7..-0.3 (assembly x 640.7) ends on the barrel plug's red stub (Wires, own z > 0, assembly z 1354.8); the one from the clip's stub at own z 0.3..1.7 (x 642.7) ends on the plug's black stub (z 1353.3). So the clip's stub at own z < 0 is red (materials.json DC_Adaptor regions). Polarity against the real clip not checked.
_conductors.servo_leads: Each FS90R carries three 1.5 mm lead stubs; Cadasio colours them brown (own x +1.1), red (0) and yellow (-1.1). On the right motor NAUO17 they sit at assembly y 907.96 / 906.86 / 905.76 (brown on top), as the CAD's own lead bodies (Fitec ... Wire Brown / Red / Yellow) have them. Both plugged leads end yellow on S, red on V, brown on G (docs/research/rcc/cad_study.md 3.3).

_skipped.note: Published RCC colours (TechBox's Cadasio project 19075) that this guide does not use, and why. 'Lee' = a ruling Lee made for the MRA that applies to the same part here; 'house' = the rulebook's colour library (docs/cadasio-patterns.md section 8).
